request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I didn't change any code: the app already does what this request asks. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` (the main "as of exports" test and scenarios 1–3).

It works because the as-of feature was built to cover the whole screen, exports included:

- **Every request carries the date.** While an as-of date is set, `api/http.ts` adds an `X-As-Of` header to every request. On the server, `AsOfFilter` answers each read as the store stood at the end of that date, and `Sheets` returns that date as the sheet's today.
- **All cached data is re-read when the date changes.** Setting or clearing the date resets every sheet query (`features/asof/asOf.slot.tsx`).
- **The exports use that same data.**
  - The people and claims exports work their figures out from the people, claims, rates and settings the screen already holds, with the as-of date as "today". That's why the people export shows Ada's due-total as 1.00 instead of 2.00 and Ben not yet retired, and why Ben's claim from 2026-03-05 is left out of the claims export.
  - The pools export re-fetches the pools when pressed, and that request carries the header too, so the cut comes out as 10.00 instead of 20.00.
- **Clearing the date brings the current figures back**, which the test also checks.
